problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨3{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2,\,2{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the acceleration is
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2,\,5+{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5+{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-8t,\,3{t}^{2}-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t-8,\,6t-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6(1)-8,\,6(1)-6⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
